draft1: Knowing anatomy alone was not enough; Victor also had to study the natural decay and corruption of the human body. Because his father had shielded him from superstition as a child, he had never trembled at ghost stories and felt no dread of the supernatural, a churchyard was, to him, simply a place holding bodies emptied of life, their former beauty reduced to food for worms. This led him to examine the process of this decay directly, spending days and nights in vaults and charnel-houses, his attention fixed on details most people would find unbearable.
